trick: Three boundaries, three outcomes. Divergent plates pull apart and make mid-ocean ridges and rift valleys; convergent plates collide and make fold mountains, trenches and volcanoes; transform plates slide past and make faults like the San Andreas. The Himalayas are convergent, the Mid-Atlantic Ridge divergent — name the boundary and the landform follows.

trick: Salinity is highest where evaporation beats rainfall and no river dilutes — so it peaks in enclosed subtropical seas, and the Dead Sea and Lake Van are the extreme cases. For currents, the rule of thumb is that warm currents flow away from the equator and cold currents flow towards it, and where they meet you get fog and the world's great fishing grounds.

video.query: ocean salinity distribution warm and cold currents class 12 geography

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the oceans.

items.statement: The average salinity of ocean water is about 35 parts per thousand.
items.why: Roughly 35 grams of dissolved salt per kilogram of sea water, of which sodium chloride is the largest part.

items.statement: Salinity is highest at the equator.
items.why: Heavy equatorial rainfall dilutes it. Salinity peaks in the subtropics, around 20° to 30°, where evaporation is high and rain is low.

items.statement: Warm currents generally flow from the equator towards the poles.
items.why: The Gulf Stream and the Kuroshio are examples; cold currents such as the Labrador and Peru flow the other way.

items.statement: The meeting of warm and cold currents produces rich fishing grounds.
items.why: Mixing brings nutrients up and supports plankton — the Grand Banks off Newfoundland is the classic case, along with dense fog.

items.statement: Tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the sun.
items.why: The moon dominates because it is far closer, though the sun reinforces it at spring tides.

chapter: Population: Density, Growth and Demographic Transition
trick: Density is people per square kilometre — arithmetic, not the same as pressure on the land. Growth rate is birth rate minus death rate, plus migration. In the demographic transition the death rate falls FIRST and the birth rate follows later, and the gap between the two falls is Stage 2, where population grows fastest.

data.prompt: Put the stages of the demographic transition in order.

items.label: Stage 1: high stationary
items.note: High birth rate and high death rate; population nearly stable, and low

items.label: Stage 2: early expanding
items.note: Death rate falls with better food and medicine while the birth rate stays high — the fastest growth

items.label: Stage 3: late expanding
items.note: The birth rate begins to fall as families choose fewer children; growth slows

items.label: Stage 4: low stationary
items.note: Both rates low; population large and nearly stable

items.label: Stage 5: declining
items.note: Birth rate below death rate; population ages and shrinks, as in parts of Europe and Japan
